author: Wanda Wilson Dooley
text: It depends on where the scan is. For example, if you're having an mri of your shoulder and your cgm is two or three inches below your shoulder, then, yes, the tech is going to make you take it off. Partially so the strongest part of the magnet isn't so close to it (it does have a metal filament in it) and partly so it does not interfere with what they want to see on the mri. In general, it's not necessary to take it off, but I don't think I'd sit there in the MRI machine and fight with the tech because if they are unwilling to do your mri, you've just wasted your time and will have to schedule another day and hope it's a different tech.
